AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should fruit be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To make it sour
   B. To make it dry
   C. To remove dirt and germs
   D. To change its colour

2. Which of these is a benefit of growing your own fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   B. Fewer vitamins
   C. Less food
   D. More expenses

3. Which nutrient in oranges and guavas helps the body to heal cuts and fight colds? (1 mark)
   A. Starch
   B. Vitamin C
   C. Salt
   D. Cooking oil

4. Which practice keeps children safe when harvesting fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Push each other
   B. Use a picking pole and take turns
   C. Pull the branch down hard
   D. Climb all trees

5. Which of these is an animal welfare need? (1 mark)
   A. Clean water always available
   B. No shelter
   C. Living in mud
   D. Being hit

6. Why should raw milk be boiled before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. To make it colder
   B. To make it thicker
   C. To kill germs
   D. To make it blue

7. Which of these can oxen do on a farm? (1 mark)
   A. Lay eggs
   B. Pull ploughs and carts
   C. Give wool
   D. Produce honey

8. Which of these is an indigenous chicken called in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Layer only
   B. Broiler
   C. Kienyeji
   D. Turkey

9. Why should we not skip breakfast? (1 mark)
   A. It makes you tired
   B. Breakfast is a waste of money
   C. The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   D. It is not real food

10. Which of these can happen if a child eats only ugali? (1 mark)
   A. Getting all vitamins
   B. Never feeling tired
   C. Growing very tall at once
   D. Feeling weak and getting sick often

11. Which meal is missing body-building foods? (1 mark)
   A. Ugali and sukuma wiki only
   B. Chapati, egg and tomato
   C. Rice, beans and cabbage
   D. Ugali, fish and spinach

12. Why is a food journal kept for a week? (1 mark)
   A. To count the number of plates
   B. To find cheap shops
   C. To check whether meals are balanced
   D. To improve handwriting only

13. Why should the frying pan be heated before adding food? (1 mark)
   A. To melt it
   B. To burn it
   C. To break it
   D. So that food browns and does not soak up oil

14. Which of these is used for boiling food? (1 mark)
   A. A frying pan only
   B. A plate
   C. A saucepan with a lid
   D. A basket

15. How do you test if boiled potatoes are cooked? (1 mark)
   A. They float
   B. They turn green
   C. A fork goes in easily
   D. They are still very hard

16. Why do we crack an egg into a bowl first? (1 mark)
   A. To check it and remove bits of shell
   B. To make it grow
   C. To cook it
   D. To make it hot

17. Should you share a toothbrush? (1 mark)
   A. Only at school
   B. Yes with friends
   C. Yes with family
   D. No

18. How often should you brush your teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Once a month
   B. Twice a day
   C. Never
   D. Once a year

19. Why should combs and towels not be shared? (1 mark)
   A. They are too big
   B. Germs and lice can spread
   C. They become dirty faster
   D. They break

20. What is the use of a hygiene log? (1 mark)
   A. Measuring rain
   B. Recording daily hygiene practices
   C. Counting money
   D. Listing games

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to plant a fruit seedling. (4 marks)

22. Explain four things that may happen to a child who does not eat a balanced diet. (4 marks)

23. Why should you brush teeth twice a day? (2 marks)

24. Prepare a balanced menu for one day for a Grade 4 child using local foods and explain why it is balanced. (5 marks)

25. Write the steps for preparing a meal using both boiling and shallow frying. Include hygiene and safety. (5 marks)

26. Explain how to make a meal of boiled potatoes and fried egg balanced. (3 marks)

27. Plan a balanced supper using local foods and name the group of each food. (3 marks)

28. Why should personal items like towels not be shared? (2 marks)

29. Give two ways of protecting fruits from birds and monkeys without killing them. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — To remove dirt and germs
   Clean fruit is safe to eat.

2. A — Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   Growing at home saves money.

3. B — Vitamin C
   Vitamin C helps the body fight illness.

4. B — Use a picking pole and take turns
   Use safe methods.

5. A — Clean water always available
   Animals need water, feed, shelter, health care and kind treatment.

6. C — To kill germs
   Boiling makes it safe.

7. B — Pull ploughs and carts
   Oxen give draught power.

8. C — Kienyeji
   Kienyeji chickens are local breeds.

9. C — The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   Breakfast gives energy for school.

10. D — Feeling weak and getting sick often
   One food cannot supply all nutrients.

11. A — Ugali and sukuma wiki only
   Ugali and kale give energy and vitamins but no protein food.

12. C — To check whether meals are balanced
   A journal shows patterns in eating.

13. D — So that food browns and does not soak up oil
   Food placed in cold oil soaks up oil.

14. C — A saucepan with a lid
   A saucepan holds water.

15. C — A fork goes in easily
   Soft potatoes are ready.

16. A — To check it and remove bits of shell
   You avoid a bad egg spoiling the pan.

17. D — No
   Toothbrushes carry germs.

18. B — Twice a day
   Morning and before bed.

19. B — Germs and lice can spread
   Personal items should be for one person.

20. B — Recording daily hygiene practices
   A log helps to form habits.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water the seedling; remove the bag carefully; place at the same depth in the hole; fill with soil and firm; water and mulch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four correct steps.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Weakness, tiredness, frequent illness, slow growth, poor concentration (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: It removes food and germs that cause decay and keeps the mouth fresh.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for removing food, 1 mark for preventing decay.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Breakfast: porridge and egg; lunch: ugali, beans and sukuma wiki; supper: rice, fish and cabbage with fruit. It includes energy, body-building and protective foods in every day.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for a menu with all groups, 2 marks for correct explanation.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands; wash food; boil potatoes until soft; shallow fry an egg or fish; serve with vegetables; safety: adult present, handles inward, dry cloth, water away from hot oil; clean up after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for hygiene, 1 for boiling, 1 for frying, 1 for safety, 1 for serving and cleaning.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes give energy and the egg gives protein. Add vegetables such as spinach or tomato for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group named.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example, rice (energy), fish (body-building), spinach (protective).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food correctly named and placed.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Germs and skin infections spread through them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for infection.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cover with nets, use scarecrows, noise or shiny objects (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
